Keeping Your Cool with Technology

For anyone whose phone, computer or printer can ruin a good mood. Each day is one small way to stay calm when tech misbehaves, set things up so they frustrate you less, and ask for help without feeling foolish.

Stress · Stress · Emotion Regulation · Self-Compassion · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Take one slow breath the next time a screen makes you wait, and let your shoulders drop as you breathe out.
  • Day 2Plug in your phone tonight in the same spot you always use, and enjoy knowing exactly where it will be in the morning.
  • Day 3Say out loud, "Everyone gets stuck with tech sometimes," and notice how it feels to give yourself that small kindness.
  • Day 4Choose, with the people you live with, a calm phrase like "tech time out" that anyone can say when a gadget raises tempers.
  • Day 5Think of one device that worked just fine for you today, and quietly thank it in your head.
  • Day 6When a web page freezes this morning, lift your hands off the keyboard and rest them in your lap for ten seconds.
  • Day 7Choose one drawer or basket near your favorite chair and make it the home for every charging cable in the house.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Name one chore that technology makes easier for you, like paying a bill from the couch, and let yourself feel glad about it.
  • Day 60Spend a winter evening with a paper book and a warm blanket, and leave the phone charging in the kitchen.
  • Day 120Keep a paper list of your important accounts' customer service numbers, without any passwords on it.
  • Day 240Admire an old radio, clock or lamp in your home that has worked for years with no fuss.
  • Day 365End the evening by plugging your phone in outside the bedroom, and let your mind settle before sleep.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
